sources.title: The Chebotarev Density Theorem
sources.version: Undated author lecture notes, five pages, retained from official Leiden mathematics site
sources.locator: Fact 2.1 and Theorem 3.1, page 3; natural-density definition and validity for both densities, pages 3-4
sources.statement: For a finite Galois extension of number fields, unramified primes in a conjugacy class have natural density equal to the class size divided by the group order. Frobenius cycle lengths on roots agree with factor degrees away from the polynomial discriminant.
sources.application: The exact all-even subset of the residual sextic's full signed-pair group has 21 of 48 elements, so the bad-prime set has density7/16. Positive density implies divergence of its reciprocal-prime sum, used in the finite-CRT product proof.
sources.reading_limits: Exact theorem, factorization/cycle statement, hypotheses and both density conventions inspected. Chebotarev itself is imported, not independently reproved. The nonmonic sextic is replaced by 9^5*g(T/9) outside3.

sources.title: Hilbert's irreducibility theorem and the larger sieve
sources.locator: Section1.1, Theorem1.2(Cohen,Serre), page2; full arithmetic-group notation, pages1-2
sources.statement: One-parameter exceptional integer specializations have count O(B^(1/2)logB), for the full arithmetic splitting group. Regularity is not a hypothesis.
sources.application: After refining any integer progression modulo a new bad prime squared, full A10 specializations remain infinite. Apply also to the compositum with previous fields over Q to obtain linear disjointness while retaining integer parameters.
sources.reading_limits: The retained exact statement and hypotheses were previously inspected and rechecked. The estimate and HIT are imported.

scope_limits: The local equivalence is for primes outside{2,3,5,13,17} dividing a nonzero integer parameter, at the zero branch. Other branch values can add restrictions.
Density7/16 concerns bad primes for the residual sextic. Densityzero concerns integer parameters for the specified rank256 subgroup product, in every fixed arithmetic progression.
The result obstructs all-parameter progression constructions, not a thinner infinite rank256 family.
All three obstructing decomposition groups have double-transposition inertia and are repaired by the H2 factor of the existing rank301 construction.
The rational-base-change obstruction only excludes killing all five finite inertia classes by an everywhere-even pullback. It does not exclude other methods of controlling decomposition groups.
The full order48 group proof uses the written real-root and complex-conjugation argument; finite counts alone do not establish the Galois group.
The finite checker does not prove Chebotarev, HIT, Hensel factorization, the infinite CRT limit, or the all-degree Riemann-Hurwitz bound.
